title: Resident transport shares are applied to incoming workers
evidence: The FSO concept is “Pendler (Weg- und Binnenpendler)”: outgoing and within-commune commuters. All 33 copied mode shares match the source, but createCityData applies them to all three flow groups. Zürich applies 16.4% MIV to incoming workers.
impact: Mode counts can be substantially biased even when their sum is correct.
action: Use direction-appropriate shares or observed OD-by-mode data. Keep resident-only shares attached to their proper population; show uncertainty for inferred pairs.

title: One journey gets different mode counts on different city pages
evidence: All 14 shared all-mode totals agree. All 14 car allocations disagree. Winterthur → Zürich: 3,430 on Winterthur’s page; 1,826 on Zürich’s page.
impact: Changing the selected city changes the inferred mode of the same commuters.
action: Allocate mode once for each origin–destination pair. Add a cross-city consistency gate, allowing a documented small rounding tolerance.

title: The Car label includes motorcycles
evidence: FSO pen_tim is motorised private transport. Geneva reproduces TRANS 4 + 5; this includes 6'655 weighted motorcycle commuters before rounding.
impact: The page cannot claim a car-only or vehicle count.
action: Label the current category “Car / motorcycle”, or acquire car-only data. Keep people distinct from vehicles and document vehicle occupancy if conversion is added.

title: No-transport records are animated as walking or cycling
evidence: All 714 French origin-mode rows reproduce exactly when soft = TRANS 1 + 2 + 3. TRANS 1 contributes 157.64 weighted people, or about 158.
impact: People reporting no journey inflate the active-travel animation and commuting population.
action: Exclude TRANS 1 from travel, keep walking and cycling separate in the import, and recalculate affected totals.

title: Walk / bike is a residual rather than a separately downloaded count
evidence: The FSO table supplies total, public transport and MIV. The project assigns total − public transport − MIV entirely to soft. No separate active category or exclusion rules were preserved.
impact: A residual may include unclassified modes; it is not evidence of bicycle counts. A distance rule then chooses walking under 3 km and cycling beyond it.
action: Verify the residual’s definition or import explicit active-mode counts. Preserve unknown modes instead of silently assigning them.

title: The population model mixes Vaud-only arrivals with all departures
evidence: OCSTAT 2024: Vaud inbound 23,398; all-canton inbound 25,628; Vaud outbound 6,881; all outbound 8,703. The model uses 23,398 and −8,703. The missing inbound group is 2,230; the extra outbound group is 1,822.
impact: Its daytime population change is about 2,230 below an all-canton construction with the same timing. The outgoing group also includes foreign or unknown workplaces, so “swissOutbound” is inaccurate.
action: Choose a consistent canton scope, add the other-canton arrivals, and distinguish Vaud, other Swiss, foreign and unknown outgoing groups.

title: Geneva uses canton flows while other pages use city communes
evidence: Geneva aggregates French workers in 45 SUC workplace communes into CH25 “Geneva workplaces”, and uses canton-level OCSTAT totals. Other city endpoints are individual communes. The INSEE file retains the real workplace communes.
impact: City-to-city totals are not directly comparable; routing canton-wide workers to central Geneva overstates particular central approaches.
action: Name the region explicitly and route French commuters to their known workplace commune. Do not compare the Geneva canton total with municipal totals as equivalent units.

title: Displayed transport modes have unequal coverage
evidence: Car routes cover at least 95% of mapped estimates in both directions. Geneva public transport covers 11'841 of 38'502 (30.8%), including both directions. Bus, foreign and transfer-dependent journeys are often missing.
impact: Dot counts and “travelling now” comparisons make modes with poor routing coverage look artificially small. Population uses broader totals.
action: Show covered / total per mode near the counter, add bus and cross-border itinerary coverage, and compare on a common denominator.

title: Long-distance active estimates survive even when their routes are excluded
evidence: 46'268 walk/bike estimates across 3'488 city-page corridors have endpoints more than 25 km apart. This is a page-row total, not unique national commuters. Examples include Lausanne → Genève and Luzern → Zürich.
impact: A uniform active share is implausible for many long journeys; hiding their geometry leaves them in the chart.
action: Use distance- and origin-specific mode evidence. Keep excluded estimates visible as uncertainty; do not reclassify them as cars without evidence.

title: The population curve is not derived from animated arrivals
evidence: On the same routed car cohort, Zürich’s sigmoid population curve differs from departure/travel-time accounting by up to 5'861 people at minute 455. This compares journey-end presence, not measured city-boundary crossings.
impact: People can be shown in transit while the independently timed curve already counts them at their destination. The curve and map cannot validate each other.
action: Use one departure/arrival event model for animation, in-transit totals and population, with a documented city-boundary rule.

title: A worker headcount is treated as a daily traffic schedule
evidence: The model schedules the full cohort each day. It has no attendance, remote-work, weekend, holiday or shift-work adjustment. Zürich has 9'228 car-category people at 07:45 and 0 at noon in this schedule.
impact: These are synthetic moments, not traffic observations. Internal trips, deliveries, shopping and through traffic are outside scope.
action: Call it an illustrative working-day commute model. Calibrate attendance and departure profiles before adding real-time or traffic claims.

title: Rail geometry is not evidence of train passengers or a valid itinerary
evidence: The importer selects a nearby station within the same commune, then a shortest rail-distance path. No timetable, transfer, service frequency, train capacity or route-specific passenger count validates the inferred PT allocation. Timing uses a coordinate-distance heuristic.
impact: PT commuters may actually use buses or other stations; the map cannot assert that they travel on the displayed train route.
action: Keep possible routes distinct from observed passenger counts; use timetable itineraries if route validity and travel time are needed.

title: Foreign origins are allocated from workplace totals
evidence: All 11 Q4 2025 workplace totals match the FSO after rounding. Their foreign home communes are nevertheless modelled allocations using selected nearby places and population/distance weights.
impact: A correct workplace total does not establish the places or routes people come from. Cross-border modal shares also inherit the resident mismatch.
action: Tag these origins as allocated; replace them with observed cross-border OD data where available and retain uncertainty elsewhere.

title: Fresh route files do not make old commuter estimates current
evidence: Swiss OD data are 2020, resident mode shares 2023, border totals Q4 2025, rail geometry 2023 and station/cache files 2026. Geographic cropping excludes some commuters before the 95% car-route target is applied.
impact: The map, chart and source totals use different denominators and vintages. There is no historical route snapshot to quantify a before/after regression.
action: Publish separate data and geometry vintages, retain dated input hashes, and show full-source → mapped → routed coverage.

title: One road endpoint snaps far from its requested location
evidence: Glarus Süd → Zürich: 18 estimated people; maximum endpoint displacement 1.64 km, against this audit’s 1 km car review threshold.
impact: A commune centroid or settlement match may put the journey on an unsuitable approach; this does not explain the city-wide low count.
action: Inspect that endpoint and choose a supported inhabited location. Keep the threshold as a review flag, not a claim of wrong traffic counts.

title: Uncertainty and parts of the original transformations are missing
evidence: FSO and OCSTAT publish uncertainty; the display rounds estimates to individual people. The checked-in city-data generator covers seven cities; the original Geneva and four earlier-city ingestion pipelines are absent. Raw source hashes and mode definitions were not carried into route caches.
impact: The existing 26 tests all pass while these definition errors remain. Regeneration and uncertainty propagation cannot be fully audited from the prior repository alone.
action: Keep the fetched source snapshots, exact filters and cohort definitions; restore missing ingestion scripts and propagate survey uncertainty. Gate future changes with this audit.
